reports.title: Elastic Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: During our last guidance, we anticipated FX rates of 1.17 against the Euro and 1.36 against the Pound. The dollar has subsequently strengthened to 1.09 against the Euro, and 1.31 against the Pound. The stronger dollar will result in a total revenue headwind of $4.5 million in Q3, and $5.0 million in Q4, a total of $9.5 million of currency-related headwind in the second half of fiscal 2027.
Against this backdrop, the Company is providing the following guidance:
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ending January 31, 2027):

•Total revenue is expected to be between $507.5 million and $508.5 million, representing 12.9% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (13.9% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $4.5 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

•Sales-led subscription revenue is expected to be between $432.0 million and $433.0 million, representing 15.1% year-over-year growth at the midpoint (16.2% year-over-year constant currency growth at the midpoint). This guidance incorporates a $4.0 million FX headwind to the midpoint.

desk.headline: Revenue up 17% to $496m and EPS $0.94, both beat; full-year EPS outlook raised despite a stronger dollar
results: Revenue grew 17% to $496m, and the company said it beat its own guidance on every key measure.
Sales-led subscription revenue rose 19% to $415m, and annual cloud contracts grew 30%.
Contracted revenue due in the next 12 months rose 19% to $1.157bn.
Adjusted operating margin reached a record 22.2%; GAAP operating profit was $22m and GAAP EPS broke even.
Elastic bought back about $55m of shares, approved a new $500m buyback, and agreed to buy HoneyHive, which tests and monitors automated AI software.

guidance.summary: Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $3.35–3.41 from $3.29–3.37, and the revenue range was narrowed around the same $2.004bn midpoint as a $9.5m currency hit offset the second-quarter beat.

points: The CFO said customer usage was strong across regions and he does not expect that to change.
Security was the fastest-growing area; about 40% of customers paying over $100,000 a year now use Elastic for AI work.
A weaker euro and pound against the dollar cut the outlook by $9.5m, and Europe and the Middle East are viewed cautiously.
HoneyHive is not expected to add much revenue this fiscal year.
The annual cloud figure will now be reported once a year, and new revenue categories start in fiscal 2028.
call.source: What Elastic (ESTC) Said on Its Q2 Earnings Call — MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 19 Nov 2026

watch: Whether currency moves eat further into the full-year revenue outlook.
Q4 renewal timing, which management expects to lift growth versus Q3.
Uptake of the new AI security and observability tools and the HoneyHive integration.
